item.title: A Look At The Biggest Events Coming To Indianapolis In 2026
item.description: With several attendance records broken and new hotel rooms added to the city, Indianapolis continues to pride itself on being one of the top destinations for conventions.

item.title: Braun Opts Into New Federal School Choice Program
item.description: Gov. Mike Braun announced Thursday, Jan. 22 that Indiana will opt into a new initiative allowing Hoosiers to collect federal tax savings for investments made in K-12 scholarships.

item.title: Syracuse Public Library – Visit Ox Bow Park With Free Park Pass
item.description: “But in every walk with nature one receives far more than he seeks,” John Muir once opined in his posthumous collection, “Steep Trails.”

item.title: Indiana Lawmaker Proposes Formal IEDC Investigation, Republicans Might Kill It
item.description: An Indiana lawmaker wants the legislature to formally investigate the embattled Indiana Economic Development Corp., but the top House Republican lawmaker who would need to sign off on the idea is splashing some cold water on the prospect.

item.title: Juror Shortage Causes Mistrial And Delay In Murder Case
item.description: Twelve jurors in Owen County were supposed to decide the fate of a 27-year-old Bloomington man whose murder trial was set to start this week.

item.title: South Bend Redevelopment Approves 2026 Money For Lincoln Park Housing
item.description: With seven houses finished and 13 under construction, the Redevelopment Commission approved a $1.25 million budget request to fund revitalization in the Lincoln Park neighborhood.

item.title: So You Want To Shovel Snow. Think About This First.
item.description: Anyone planning to shovel the snow that is almost certain to blanket the region this weekend may want to know what the American Heart Association says about that.

item.title: eBay’s buyer protection loophole leaves a customer empty-handed
item.description: Joe Burley buys a mini PC on eBay, but the seller ships his package to another address.

item.title: Anti-Grooming Legislation Would Expand The Places Child Predators Cannot Go
item.description: leo Collins told the Senate Corrections and Criminal Law Committee on Tuesday, Jan. 20 that her 5-year-old daughter was groomed by a child predator- “slowly, deliberately through repeated contact that made her trust someone who shouldn’t have had access to her in the first place.”

item.title: Girl Scout Summer Camp Registration Now Open
item.description: Registration is now open for Girl Scouts of Northern Indiana-Michiana summer camp programs.
